title: Bioorthogonal catalytic materials for precise chemical control in living systems
content: Bioorthogonal catalysis enables highly selective chemical transformations in living systems, but the limited stability, biosafety, and spatiotemporal controllability of free catalysts restrict their broader biomedical applications. Bioorthogonal catalytic materials provide a potential solution by integrating catalytic activity with the structural programmability, protective functions, and responsive properties of biomaterials. In this review, we establish a systematic framework connecting catalytic reactions, material design, spatiotemporal regulation, and biomedical functions. We focus on how different catalytic reactions define the requirements for material construction, as well as how exogenous transition metal catalysts and endogenous metal resources can be introduced, stabilized, and regulated within material systems. On this basis, we further summarize the spatiotemporal control of catalytic processes by endogenous signals, external stimuli, and multi-stimuli responsive systems, and discuss representative applications in protein engineering, disease diagnosis, cancer therapy, and noncancer disease treatment. Finally, we outline the major challenges that remain in biosafety, catalytic mechanisms, materials engineering, dosing and pharmacokinetics, disease adaptation, and clinical translation. With a deeper understanding of catalytic behavior, material structure, and in vivo processes, bioorthogonal catalytic materials are expected to enable more precise chemical control of complex living systems and facilitate broader clinical translation.
